question: A 50-year-old woman with a prosthetic mitral valve presents with fever and new splinter haemorrhages. Blood cultures are ordered for suspected infective endocarditis. Which collection approach is CORRECT?

answers.text: Collect 3 sets from 3 separate venepuncture sites within 1–2 hours before starting antibiotics

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. In IE, bacteraemia is continuous (not intermittent), so 3 sets from 3 separate peripheral sites within 1–2 hours maximises sensitivity and helps distinguish true bacteraemia from skin contaminants. Each set includes aerobic + anaerobic bottles.

answers.text: Wait for the next fever spike before collecting blood to maximise yield

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Bacteraemia in IE is continuous — it is NOT related to fever spikes. There is no benefit to timing collection with temperature rises. Collect cultures at any time; do not delay for a spike.

answers.text: Draw all 3 sets from an existing central venous catheter to minimise patient discomfort

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Catheter-drawn cultures have unacceptably high contamination rates. Peripheral venepuncture from 3 separate sites is essential to distinguish true bacteraemia from catheter colonisation or skin flora.

answers.text: Refrigerate culture bottles immediately after collection to preserve fastidious organisms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Blood culture bottles must be transported at body temperature or room temperature — never refrigerated. Cold temperatures kill fastidious organisms such as HACEK group bacteria, reducing diagnostic yield.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the protocol: 3 sets from 3 separate venepuncture sites (not catheters), collected within 1–2 hours, transported at body temperature (not refrigerated), before starting empirical antibiotics.

Key principles: IE bacteraemia is continuous → timing irrelevant; 3 sets × 3 sites → sensitivity + contaminant discrimination; inoculate aerobic bottle first; transport at body temperature; load into BACTEC/BacT/ALERT system promptly.
